analysis_notes.note: Torah #115 is a short personal narrative (sippur) about Rebbe Nachman's practice of choosing a path of avodas Hashem and firmly persisting in it without being distracted by competing thoughts. The text contains no bechina (parallel-aspect) statements at all. It is purely advisory/narrative, describing a personal practice of hischazekus (strengthening) and consistency. No conceptual mappings of the form 'X is a bechina of Y' are present, and thus no packages, additions, or new bechina edges can be proposed.
